terms.gloss: a chore, a day’s set task
terms.comment: Anciently a day’s weight of wool to spin.

phrases.english: Of course I do some chores at home.

phrases.latin: Multum hodiē domī negōtiī est: tū verrēs, ego vāsa lavābō.
phrases.english: There’s a lot to do at home today: you’ll sweep, and I’ll wash the dishes.

phrases.latin: nihil opust nōbīs ancillā nisi quae texat, quae molat, lignum caedat, pēnsum faciat, aedīs verrat … quae habeat cottīdiānum familiae coctum cibum
phrases.english: we need no maid except one to weave, grind the corn, chop wood, do her day’s spinning, sweep the house … and have the household’s daily food cooked

phrases.latin: Munda siet: vīllam conversam mundēque habeat; focum pūrum circumversum cotīdiē, priusquam cubitum eat, habeat.
phrases.english: She must be clean herself: let her keep the house swept and clean, and the hearth clean and swept round every day before she goes to bed.

sources: Lewis & Short: pensum

Morgan–Owens, Adumbratio: s.v. clean house, clean up, tidy up, broom: dustpan, garbage, trash, garbage can, waste basket. John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, pp. 38, 39, 40, 52, 290, 292, 307, 320, 401, 404.
